narrative:
On October 12, 2026, the Karnataka High Court listed 2,965 cases across 50 judges and conducted hearings in 1,356 matters, achieving an overall hearing rate of 45.7%. This marks a recovery from the 42.6% rate recorded on October 9 (1,150 of 2,701 heard) and approaches the 46.1% rate logged on October 8 (1,393 of 3,021 heard), sustaining the court's recent band between 40% and 47%.

Individual bench output diverged substantially across courtrooms. In Hall 22, Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar maintained consistent productivity, hearing 41 of 53 matters (77.4%) and 54 of 69 matters (78.3%) across two sessions. Justice V. Srishananda in Hall 23 heard 63 of 87 listed cases (72.4%), while Justice G. Basavaraja in Hall 32 addressed 70 of 106 cases (66.0%). Conversely, concentrated caseloads created bottlenecks; Justice B. M. Shyam Prasad heard 9 of 148 matters (6.1%) on his primary Hall 7 roster, despite clearing 15 of 16 matters (93.8%) on a smaller list.

Across procedural stages, Preliminary Hearings led major lists with a 56.5% hearing rate (229 of 405), followed by Admissions at 51.9% (351 of 676) and Orders at 47.1% (455 of 966). Conversion for both Orders and Admissions improved compared to October 9 levels (41.8% and 46.2%, respectively). Substantive stages progressed more slowly: Final Hearings converted 30.4% (190 of 626), and Further Hearings reached just 18.3% (17 of 93).

Writ Petitions dominated aggregate scheduling with 1,451 cases, converting at 39.5% (573 heard). Criminal dockets demonstrated higher throughput, as Criminal Petitions recorded 57.5% (275 of 478) and Criminal Appeals reached 61.6% (114 of 185). Miscellaneous First Appeals converted 54.9% (174 of 317), contrasting sharply with Regular First Appeals, which resolved only 18.7% (17 of 91).
